Retrieval_System_Blueprint.description: Retriever catalog optimized for LOCOMO dataset - conversational memory about personal events, temporal queries, and speaker-specific information.

dataset_context.name: Locomo
dataset_context.description: Conversational dialogues with personal memory questions

bm25.description: Keyword-based (Okapi BM25) search. Ranks by term frequency and inverse document frequency. Best for exact name/term matches.
strengths: Perfect for finding exact names (Caroline, Melanie, specific places)
Excellent when query contains unique keywords (LGBTQ, medication names)
limitations: WARNING: Fails if the exact keywords are not present.
DO NOT USE for conceptual questions, even if they contain a keyword (e.g., a query about 'research' may not be answered by a doc that says 'looking into').

faiss.description: Vector-based semantic search (FAISS). Finds conceptually similar documents, even without keyword overlap.
strengths: Best for conceptual or open-ended questions (e.g., 'What fields... pursue?')
limitations: May fail on abstract concepts (e.g., 'identity') if the embedding model can't connect them.
Can be 'distracted' by semantically similar but irrelevant documents.

ensemble.description: Hybrid search. Combines keyword (BM25) and semantic (FAISS) results. A strong, reliable default.
strengths: Best of both worlds: catches exact keywords AND understands concepts.
Excellent safe default when a query is mixed or unclear.
limitations: Slightly slower as it runs two retrievers.

self_query.description: An 'intelligent' retriever that uses an LLM to extract metadata filters from the query *before* searching.
strengths: ESSENTIAL for speaker-specific questions (e.g., 'What did *Caroline* say?').
Translates natural language ('yesterday', 'last week') into date filters.
Filters by speaker, date, or session.

multiquery.description: A 'query expansion' retriever. Uses an LLM to rewrite a single query into multiple variations, increasing the chance of a match.
strengths: Excellent for ambiguous or abstract queries (e.g., 'What is Caroline's identity?' might become 'Who is Caroline?', 'Caroline's personal details', 'Caroline gender identity').
limitations: Can sometimes add noise if variations are poor.

parent_document.description: Context-aware retriever. Finds small, relevant chunks and then retrieves the full session document they belong to.
strengths: Best for broad, summary-style questions (e.g., 'What was the main topic of the meeting?')
Provides full context to the LLM.

mmr.description: Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR). A semantic search (FAISS) that also tries to pick *diverse* documents to avoid repetition.
strengths: Good for 'brainstorming' or 'exploratory' queries (e.g., 'What are all the things they discussed?')
Avoids 10 documents all saying the same thing.
limitations: May intentionally skip a relevant document if it's too similar to one already selected.

examples: When did Caroline go to the LGBTQ support group?

speaker_specific_queries.description: Query asks what a specific person said or did.

identity_relationships.description: Query asks 'Who' someone is or their relationship.

conceptual_questions.description: Query asks for an opinion, summary, or inference.
examples: What fields would Caroline be likely to pursue?
